name: Blocks Product Editor for WooCommerce
author: ethereumicoio

sections.description:
Blocks Product Editor for WooCommerce plugin enables the Gutenberg Editor for WooCommerce products.

WooCommerce shipped its own block-based product editor and then removed it in 11.0 with no replacement, so a product description is edited in the classic editor again. This plugin brings the WordPress block editor back to the product screen: every product, its description, its short description and the product taxonomies are edited with blocks, and the classic editor is one switch away when a shop needs it.

Works with the WooCommerce versions that still ship a product block template (7.7 – 10.x) as well as with 11.0 and newer, which have none – the plugin only edits that template away where it exists.

Features

Every claim below has its own frame in this gallery.

  • Edit a product’s description, short description and taxonomies in the WordPress block editor, with prices, stock and third-party boxes still in the product data panel.
  • Type the regular price and the sale price on the block editor screen, without switching to the classic editor.
  • Set the SKU, the tracked stock, the backorder choice and the “sold individually” flag in the same panel as before.
  • Keep WooCommerce‘s own Variations tab on the free build: the attributes, prices and stock of every variation stay editable where they always were.
  • See and change the product’s “Catalog visibility” and “Featured” flag in the editor sidebar, where WooCommerce‘s classic Publish box no longer reaches.
  • Turn the block editor on for products with one switch, and read a diagnostics report of this install – WooCommerce and its version, the block editor, the measured plugins – with a status and what to do next for every row.
  • Never lose a variation description written with blocks: the classic variations screen shows it as a readable preview, and one button turns it back into plain text, formatting dropped.
  • Send a single product back to the classic editor from its own screen, while the rest of the shop keeps blocks.

PRO Features

Every claim below has its own frame in this gallery. These come with the PRO licence, and the free build keeps them visible but locked.

  • Edit a product’s price, sale price, SKU and stock in a fields panel in the editor sidebar.
  • Edit the attributes, SKU, price, sale price, stock and image of every variation in one table.
  • Select several variations and write the same value into all of them in one request.
  • Choose a variation’s image from the media library straight in its row.
  • Decide which user roles and which product types get the block editor – shop managers, for example, can keep the classic screen.
  • Edit the product short description in the full WordPress editor instead of a plain textarea.
  • Pick each variation attribute from a list in its row, including “Any …” for an attribute a variation leaves open.
  • Edit a variation’s description with the full block editor in a modal window.

sections.changelog:
1.7.0

  • New: “Catalog visibility” and “Featured” are now free for everyone – the control lives in the block editor sidebar for every shop, editable, with no licence and no upgrade prompt. The classic screen keeps it in its Publish box, so the block screen showing it too is the same level rather than an extra.
  • New: the plugins screen now warns when an active plugin cannot work with the block editor’s variations table, naming it and linking to the diagnostics report – so the conflict is visible before a product is opened. Plugins that keep working are not reported.

1.6.1

  • Changed: the fields panel in the editor sidebar now also edits the product attributes, the upsell and
    cross-sell links, and the weight and dimensions – everything the same panel already did for price, stock
    and SKU.
  • Changed: the plugin page lists features and Professional features in their own sections, so the free and
    the paid capabilities are told apart at a glance.
  • Fixed: refreshed the translation template and the bundled translations.

1.6.0

  • New: the per-product switch is now free for everyone – one product can go back to the classic editor while
    the rest of the shop keeps the block editor. It is not sold on purpose: the way out of a screen that broke
    on a single product is not something a shop should have to buy a licence for.
  • Note: the “Per-product switch” row on the settings page was removed. It never did anything – nothing read
    it and nothing saved it – so there is no global setting for this switch to turn on or off.
